Most typical changes considered by the research are the changes in the distribution of the reward R R , changes in the transition probability function P P , and changes in the distribution of the action space A A . Even though in the general case all MDP elements can have time dependence, we are not aware of the work that studies these settings. A number of studies that investigate adaptation to non-stationarity try to modify the Markov decision process model so that it can better reflect non-stationarity. These works can be divided into two groups: POMDP-based and MDP-based methods. The first group uses the partially observable Markov decision process (POMDP), the framework proposed by Åström Åström ( 1965 ) and later developed by Kaelbling Kaelbling et al. ( 1998 ) . This is a broad framework that allows the representation of uncertainty and non-stationarity of the environment, when non-stationarity can be seen as the agent’s understanding of the environment rather than the property of the environment. The broad nature of the POMDP makes it attractive for modeling non-stationarity on a high level, but brings some difficulties in implementation. There were several efforts to extend POMDP to simplify its implementation for nonstationary environments. Choi et. al Choi et al.
